slides.narration: Chapter 16: The Mass Spectrum. Every particle mass — from the nearly massless electron to the heavy top quark — is a specific screening pattern on the golden-ratio tower, derived from zero free parameters.

In the tower, heavier particles sit closer to the frontier — less screened, more visible. Lighter particles are deeper in the tower — more screened, more hidden. The mass of each particle is determined by how many layers of golden-ratio screening it sits behind.

The Higgs boson mass comes out to 125.25 GeV — matching the measured value to within a tenth of a standard deviation. This is not from fitting parameters to data. It is from the tower's self-referential fixed-point equation, where the mass appears in its own formula.
